title: Audit log export: role-aware filtered dump (2026)
author: Aisha Rahman
body:
## Overview
This document specifies the Console and API capability to export filtered slices of tenant audit logs as a bulk dump while enforcing RBAC v2, retention limits, and SSO-backed administrative permissions.

The primary use cases are compliance reporting, e-discovery preparation, and offline analytics. The design explicitly prevents disclosure of sensitive fields to users without the appropriate allow-list role.

## Scope
### In scope
- Role-aware bulk export for audit logs, initiated from Console (Admin) and backed by a server-side export worker.
- Query-scoped exports: time window, actor, resource, action, outcome.
- Field-level masking and omission using RBAC v2 policy evaluation.
- Export bundles include a manifest describing query, filters, snapshot time, and schema version.
- Support for multi-GB exports using cursor-based pagination and resumable multipart downloads.
- Export request auditing to an immutable audit stream separate from the exported data.

### Out of scope
- Real-time streaming feeds for customer SIEMs (handled by the Audit Streaming project).
- Interactive “preview rows” in Console (removed; see decision ADR-EXPORT-004 below).

## User experience (Console)
1. Admin navigates to: Console → Security → Audit Logs → Export.
2. Admin configures filters (time range required; other filters optional).
3. Console shows:
   - Estimated record count and approximate size (best-effort)
   - Retention cutoff date for the tenant
   - Whether any sensitive fields may be included (based on role)
4. Admin submits export request.
5. Console shows export status: queued → running → completed/failed.
6. On completion, Console provides a time-limited download link and checksum.

## Data security and access control
### Authentication and identity
- Requester identity is derived from SSO/SAML session (Console) or service token (API).
- The exported bundle records requester identity in the immutable audit stream (not inside the bundle manifest).

### Authorization model
RBAC v2 is enforced server-side for every exported row.

Permissions:
- audit.export.create: can initiate exports
- audit.export.read: can view export status and download links for exports they initiated
- audit.export.read_all: can view exports initiated by other admins within the same tenant
- audit.export.sensitive_fields: can receive fields classified as Sensitive (PII / payload bodies / tokens)

Field handling rules:
- Default: sensitive fields are omitted entirely (not present) rather than present-but-null.
- If audit.export.sensitive_fields is present, sensitive fields are included, subject to any additional policy constraints.

### Retention and legal holds
- Exports cannot retrieve records older than the tenant retention cutoff.
- The previous “super-admin retention override” is deprecated.
- New approach (2026-03 update): retrieval beyond standard retention requires an explicit Legal Hold, represented by a legal_hold_id, and is only allowed for tenants with Legal Hold enabled.
- All uses of legal_hold_id are logged to the immutable audit stream with ticket reference.

## Export formats
Supported formats (2026-03 update):
- NDJSON (recommended/default): line-delimited JSON objects
- CSV: RFC 4180-ish with quoted fields and stable column order

Not supported:
- “Pretty JSON array” export (removed due to memory pressure and poor incremental handling).

## Export bundle structure
Each export produces a bundle containing:
- data.ndjson OR data.csv (may be split into multiple parts)
- manifest.json
- checksums.txt

Multipart behavior:
- Exports larger than 1.0 GB are produced as multiple numbered parts (part-0001, part-0002, ...).
- Download is resumable using HTTP range requests.

## Manifest contents (manifest.json)
The manifest is designed to support downstream compliance workflows without leaking sensitive data.

Fields (conceptual):
- schema_version: string (e.g., "2026-03-18")
- snapshot_time: RFC3339 timestamp when the export job started reading
- tenant_id: internal tenant identifier
- requested_by: NOT included (identity is captured in immutable audit log)
- query: normalized filters (time window, actor/resource/action/outcome)
- applied_rbac_policy_hash: hash of effective RBAC v2 policy used for evaluation
- retention_cutoff: timestamp
- output_format: "ndjson" | "csv"
- part_count: integer
- total_records: integer (best-effort)
- warnings: array of strings (e.g., "Some fields omitted due to RBAC")

## Backend design
### High-level flow
1. Console calls Export API to create an export job.
2. API validates permissions, normalizes query, enforces retention/hold rules.
3. API writes an export job record and enqueues work.
4. Export worker reads audit events in deterministic order, applies RBAC masking/omission, and streams output to object storage.
5. Worker writes manifest + checksums and marks job complete.
6. API returns a presigned download URL (time-limited) when requested.

### Storage and encryption
- Data is streamed directly to object storage using multipart upload to avoid memory pressure.
- Encryption:
  - In transit: TLS
  - At rest: object storage server-side encryption (SSE) plus KMS key per environment
- Presigned download link TTL (2026-03 update): 4 hours default; configurable per plan tier (max 24 hours).

### Query and pagination
- Use cursor-based incremental listing to avoid deep OFFSET scans.
- Cursor format: <event_ts_ms>|<event_id>
- Ordering: (event_ts asc, event_id asc) to ensure deterministic traversal during concurrent writes.

### Masking and serialization
- RBAC v2 policy evaluation happens before serialization.
- Sensitive fields are dropped unless audit.export.sensitive_fields is granted.
- Additional gating (separate allow-list) applies to:
  - request_payload
  - response_content
  - ip_address (masked by default; last octet removed unless sensitive_fields granted)

## Limits and quotas
| Limit | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Max concurrent exports per org | 1 | 2026-03 update (was 2) to reduce peak load |
| Max export lookback | Retention cutoff | Extended lookback requires legal_hold_id |
| Max parts per export | 2,000 | Prevent runaway multipart bundles |
| Rate limit: create export | 5 / hour / org | Burst allowed up to 2 within 5 minutes |

## Telemetry and auditing
Telemetry events:
- audit_export_created
- audit_export_started
- audit_export_completed
- audit_export_failed

Notes:
- Telemetry includes tokenized requester ID (for correlation) and tenant ID.
- A separate immutable audit stream records:
  - requester identity (SSO subject or service token)
  - export job id
  - query summary (redacted)
  - whether sensitive fields were included
  - whether legal_hold_id was used and associated ticket reference

## Operational runbook (high level)
### Common failures
- Object storage multipart upload failures: retry with exponential backoff; ensure worker has sufficient egress.
- Policy evaluation timeouts: reduce batch size and ensure policy cache is warm.
- Retention violations: confirm tenant retention and whether Legal Hold is enabled.

### On-call checks
- Dashboard: audit-export-metrics (queue depth, completion latency, failures)
- Verify KMS permissions for export worker identity
- Confirm org-level concurrency gate is functioning

## Testing and QA
- Synthetic large dataset test: 50M rows for cursor stability and throughput.
- RBAC masking matrix: org-admin, security-reader, billing-admin, auditor_role.
- Resumable download test: interrupt mid-download and resume via range requests.
- Security review: ensure no indirect disclosure via manifest, filenames, or error messages.

## Key decisions and changes
- ADR-EXPORT-001: Background worker + presigned link chosen over synchronous generation.
- ADR-EXPORT-002: Cursor (time+id) chosen over offset-based pagination.
- ADR-EXPORT-003: NDJSON recommended for JSON-like exports to support streaming parsers.
- ADR-EXPORT-004 (2026-03 update): Removed “preview first 500 rows” from Console due to data leakage risk and inconsistent RBAC UX; replaced with size estimate + schema description.
- ADR-EXPORT-005 (2026-03 update): Deprecated super-admin retention override; replaced with Legal Hold workflow using legal_hold_id and mandatory audit trail.

## Ownership
Primary owner team: Security (Audit & Compliance).
Implementation team: Engineering (Security-Logging-Initiative).
